question.problem:
The following table gives the speed of a minivan measured during a $4$-second interval.

| $t\,(\text{seconds})$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)\,(\text{meters/second})$ | $17$ | $18$ | $k$ | $25$ | $27$ |

 If the right Riemann sum approximation of the total distance that the minivan traveled during the $4$-second interval has a value of $85$ meters, what is the value of $k?$

*Hint: The distance traveled is given by the area under the speed-time graph.*
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the curve $y=v(t)$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{v(1)+v(2)+v(3)+v(4)}})\cdot {{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $v(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)$ | $18$ | $k$ | $25$ | $27$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(18+k+25+27)\cdot 1 \\  & =70+k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total distance that the minivan traveled. Since we are given that the right Riemann sum approximation of the total distance is $85$ meters,  we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}70+k & =85 \\ k & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
